spans.note: suppress warnings; set RNG seed for reproducibility
section header: DATA LOADING AND PREPARATION

spans.operation: load the raw player-referee dyad dataset from a fixed CSV path as the analysis scope
average the two raters' skin-tone scores into one continuous skinTone measure
drop dyads with no skin tone rating from the working frame
collapse red card counts into a binary any-red-card outcome
dichotomize continuous skin tone into dark/light indicators at three candidate cutpoints, designating 0.25 as primary
derive player age relative to a fixed reference year (2013) from birthdate
z-score standardize height, weight, age, and the two implicit/explicit bias measures for modeling
restrict the analytic sample to complete cases on position, physical, and bias covariates

spans.note: report final sample size, unique players/referees, and event count

spans.operation: one-hot encode position and league, dropping the first level as reference
choose and assemble the covariate adjustment set (skin-tone indicator, standardized physical/behavioral/bias covariates, position and league dummies, intercept) for the regression
fit a logistic regression of any-red-card on the covariate set with standard errors clustered by referee
pull out the dark-skin coefficient, clustered SE, two-sided p-value, and 95% CI as the reported effect
convert the log-odds coefficient and its CI into an odds ratio for reporting
compute an adjusted risk difference via marginal standardization: set the dark indicator to 1/0 for all dyads, predict probabilities under each counterfactual, and contrast their means
approximate the risk difference's uncertainty with a delta-method SE, build a Wald 95% CI, and derive a two-sided z-test p-value

spans.note: print risk difference, CI, p-value, and prose interpretation

spans.operation: refit the primary logistic model substituting alternative dark-skin cutpoints (0.375, 0.5) as a robustness check
restrict the sample to dyads with at least 2 games as a robustness check
refit the clustered logistic model on the games-restricted subsample

spans.note: print restricted-sample size and sensitivity result

spans.operation: label the switch to a Poisson count-outcome specification with exposure offset
model red-card counts with a Poisson GLM using log(games) as an exposure offset and dropping games as a direct covariate, with SEs clustered by referee

spans.note: print Poisson coefficient/SE/p/IRR and conclusion banner

spans.operation: frame the final conclusion as the adjusted risk difference and two-sided p-value (α=0.05) supporting the hypothesis that referees give more red cards to dark-skinned players, citing consistency across sensitivity analyses
